classroom.title: Course materials are on Google Classroom
classroom.text: Lecture notes, tutorials, quizzes and announcements for this course are posted on Google Classroom: one class for the lectures and one for tutorials and quizzes. Registered students received both class codes in the first lecture. If you do not have them, email the instructor.

about.text: This first course in mathematics covers the basics of linear algebra: vector spaces, matrix algebra, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, orthogonality, symmetric and positive definite matrices, and the singular value decomposition. It builds the foundation in linear algebra used later in both the CSE and ECE curricula, introduces some applications in engineering as time permits, and develops mathematical maturity through proofs and rigour.

weeklyPlan.note: Planned order of topics, following the IIIT Delhi course description. The pace may change a little during the semester.

units.title: Linear systems and matrices
weeks: Systems of linear equations; row reduction and echelon forms
Vector equations and the matrix equation Ax = b; solution sets of linear systems
Matrix operations; the inverse of a matrix; characterizations of invertible matrices

units.title: Vector spaces
weeks: Linear dependence and independence; bases and dimension
The fundamental subspaces (column, null and row spaces); rank–nullity; applications

units.title: Linear transformations and determinants
weeks: Linear transformations; kernel, range and rank; algebra of linear transformations
Matrix of a linear transformation; effect of change of basis; similarity
Determinants and their properties; Cramer's rule; determinants as volume

units.title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
weeks: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors; the characteristic equation
Diagonalization; eigenvectors and linear transformations; complex eigenvalues

units.title: Orthogonality and symmetric matrices
weeks: Inner product, length and orthogonality; orthogonal projections; Gram–Schmidt process and QR decomposition; least squares
Diagonalization of symmetric matrices; quadratic forms and positive definite matrices; singular value decomposition; application to image processing

gradingNotes: Quizzes: three quizzes of 10 marks each (30 marks).
Mid-semester examination: 25 marks. End-semester examination: 40 marks.
Tutorials: 5 marks for attending at least 8 tutorial sessions. No relaxation will be given for any reason.

policies.title: Electronic devices
policies.text: Mobile phones, laptops and tablets may not be used during lectures or tutorial sessions.

policies.title: Getting help
policies.text: If you are struggling with the material, email the instructor, the Teaching Fellow or the teaching assistants, or come to office hours. Ask early rather than letting doubts accumulate.
